exposure: time since delivery (0-6 months vs. 7-12 months)
outcome: sexual dysfunction (measured by the Female Sexual Function Index)
Female Sexual Function Index scores across all subdomains
cohort: 142 women who had given birth in the past year, were currently breastfeeding, and had not experienced postpartum depression
finding: Vaginal delivery and cesarean section were not significantly different in terms of sexual functioning one year postpartum, except for a short period of time in the early postpartum stage (0-6 months).
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with lower scores on all Female Sexual Function Index subdomains except for desire during the first 6 months postpartum compared to 7-12 months postpartum.
